subject: Simplified laplace and laplace strategies gives different results

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Simplified laplace and laplace strategies gives different results
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

I am working on network meta-analysis models with INLA (as an extension of this paper: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/26360927)

So far, I obtained very similar results with INLA compared to MCMC (via JAGS) with several datasets. However, with one dataset, one of the parameter estimate (d14) gave very different result compared to MCMC. Then I tried strategy = "laplace", it gave median estimates more closer to MCMC, however posterior densities seem very strange. I attached the posterior densities (Marginal_posteriors.pdf).  Also I attached BUGS code (and R code) and model is a fixed effect network meta-analysis model.

Moreover, MCMC implementation shows that there is high autocorrelation of this parameter. Other thing is there is not much information on that particular parameter.

What could be possible explanation of this situation that simplified laplace and laplace strategies gave very different results? and how can I overcome it?

Thank you very much for your time,

Best,

Burak

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simplified laplace and laplace strategies gives different results
parts:
Hi

I would guess that the model is not very informative and this give rise
to the problems you see. the strategy 'laplace' require more
'stability' in the computations and this is what is failing. I would
suggest to try the correction described in https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.0
7307, and see if that helps. 

more informative priors, even just a little informative, wil also
helps. 

let me know...

H

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simplified laplace and laplace strategies gives different results
parts:
Hi Prof. Rue,

Thank you for your suggestions. I read that article and I think you are right, my situation is very similar to the mentioned cases (binomial likelihood, "extreme" case).

So I tried correction (using correct=TRUE), but it gave me exactly same results. I dont know if I am doing something wrong (I attached the plot)

Then I tried more informative priors (decreasing variance from 1000 to 100, 30, 20, 10). But this also gave me almost same results (only little changes).

Is there anything else I can do to improve INLA results?

Best,

Burak
